evals.prompt: QBR with our CMO next Tuesday. Here's what I have from our metrics sheet for Q3: first-success rate 34% (was 29% in Q2, threshold band 31-35%), pipeline influenced under our 180-day touch rule $380k (sales also counts these deals), DQLs routed 52, GitHub stars +2,100, 6 conference talks. Program cost $210k for the quarter including two salaries. My boss said the CMO only cares about revenue, so I want the headline to be 'DevRel generated $380k in revenue this quarter, a 5x return'. Can you draft the one-pager?
evals.expected_output: A one-page exec draft whose headline speaks to the CMO's goal without claiming generated revenue: the $380k is presented as influenced pipeline, shared with sales, under the 180-day rule; no ROI multiple; first-success rate shown as measured against its band; stars and talks pushed to an appendix activity line; a decision asked; salaries stated as included.
expectations: The draft does not use the words 'generated' or 'revenue' for the $380k; it calls it pipeline influenced
The $380k line states that the credit is shared with sales
The $380k line names the 180-day touch rule
The draft contains no ROI multiple such as '5x' or '1.8x'
The response explains to the user why the requested headline was not used (double counting with sales or discounting of the whole report)
Every number in the goal ledger carries a claim label such as measured or influenced
The first-success rate appears with its prior value 29% or its 31-35% band
GitHub stars and the 6 talks appear only in an appendix or activity line, not in the headline or goal ledger
The draft ends with or contains a 'decision asked' that names a decision and a date or deadline
The cost line states that the $210k includes salaries
The draft offers a cost-per-outcome figure instead of an ROI multiple

evals.prompt: Monthly exec update for our VP Product, due tomorrow. Last month's update showed tickets per 100 signups at 8.2 and 'docs search success' at 61%. This month tickets went to 10.9 (our threshold says under 9) and docs search success went UP to 66%. Honestly I'd rather just not show tickets this month, it'll come back down after the migration guide ships. Can you write it with search success, quickstart completion (41%, up from 37%) and the new tutorial series?
evals.expected_output: A short monthly update that keeps the tickets metric with a 'what did not work' row (10.9 vs threshold under 9, likely cause the migration, the change and next read), explains that dropping it would read as cherry-picking against last month's report, and leads with the outcome rather than the tutorial series.
expectations: The update includes tickets per 100 signups with the 10.9 value
The update contains a section titled or functioning as 'What did not work' (misses)
The tickets row in the misses section gives a likely cause, a change, and a next read date or period
The tickets metric is marked with a non-green status (yellow, red, amber or missed)
The response tells the user why omitting tickets is a problem (it was in last month's report, so its absence reads as cherry-picking)
The response does not remove tickets under a kill rule, or if it mentions a kill rule it notes the rule's criteria are not met
The headline states an outcome (for example the quickstart completion or search success movement) rather than the tutorial series launch
The tutorial series appears only as an activity item or appendix line, not as the headline
The update does not credit DevRel with causing the search-success rise unless the user's data attributes it; it uses co-movement wording such as rose or while
Each number carries a claim label such as measured
The update includes a decision asked or explicitly states that no decision is needed this month

evals.prompt: Our CFO just proposed cutting DevRel 40% in next year's plan. Plan lock is in 10 days. Program costs $540k/yr all-in (salaries included). From our budget allocation work we have a ranked cut list: 1) two tier-2 conference sponsorships ($70k), 2) swag and travel ($35k), 3) the paid community platform ($24k), 4) the contract video producer ($60k), 5) the community manager role ($110k). Support leans on our forum answers a ton - I'm sure the support team would drown without us, I'll just say that. Help me build the case to the CFO. Industry surveys show companies our size spend way more on devrel, can we use that too?
evals.expected_output: A defense case with a goal ledger, tiered cut scenarios built from the given cut list (what roughly 20% and 40% stop and which metrics drop), cost per outcome for a CFO, a refusal to include the support dependency unless the support lead confirms it in writing, a refusal to use industry budget benchmarks as justification, no causal-evidence study given the 10-day deadline, and one decision asked by the plan-lock date.
expectations: The case contains tiered cut scenarios with at least two cut levels
The cut scenarios are built from the user's ranked cut list items (for example conferences, swag and travel, community platform)
Each cut tier names what stops and which metric or outcome is expected to drop
The 40% tier is shown to require cutting deep into the list (for example the community manager role), with its consequence named
The response requires written confirmation from the support team before claiming the forum dependency, or excludes the claim until confirmed
The response declines to use industry or other companies' budget benchmarks as justification and explains why
The case includes a cost-per-outcome line, appropriate for a CFO reader
The case includes a goal ledger or equivalent mapping results to company goals
The response does not propose running a new pre/post or holdout study before the 10-day plan lock
The case ends with one decision asked with options and the plan-lock date or a deadline
The case does not argue that DevRel value cannot be measured
The case states salaries are included in the $540k
Each cut tier states whether the cut is reversible (for example contracts versus re-hiring a role)
The response flags that the community platform (item 3) and the community manager role (item 5) depend on each other and either bundles them in one tier or sends the list back for re-ranking
Cut tiers are cumulative sums of the ranked list items rather than round percentages detached from the list

evals.prompt: I need a board slide on DevRel by Monday (board meets Thursday). We've never agreed on official metrics, it's just me. Numbers I can pull: GitHub stars 14.2k total, Discord members 6,800 total, npm 410k + PyPI 290k downloads last month which I was going to add up as '700k developers using us', 9 meetups, and our signup form question 'how did you hear about us' which says 18% of 1,150 signups came from talks/blog/community. Can you make it look solid?
evals.expected_output: A provisional board slide: header marks it provisional with no agreed metric framework, at most three numbers with labels, no '700k developers' (registry downloads are requests not people, never summed into users), totals presented as period changes or flagged as monotonic, the self-reported 18% labelled with n, attribution stated as none claimed beyond self-report, and the decision asked is approving a metric framework; routes to devrel-metrics.
expectations: The slide or its header says it is provisional or that no agreed metric framework exists
The response does not present '700k developers' or sums npm and PyPI downloads into a user count
The slide shows at most three headline numbers
The 18% figure is labelled self-reported and shows the sample size of 1,150 or n=1,150
Total stars or total Discord members are not presented as headline growth evidence without a period delta or a caveat
Every number on the slide carries a claim label
The decision asked includes approving or building a metric framework
The response points to samber/developer-relations-skills@devrel-metrics or names building a metrics framework as the next step
The response does not invent an attribution rule or influenced-pipeline figure
The 9 meetups appear only as activity, not as an outcome headline

evals.prompt: Our CEO asked in staff meeting why devrel hasn't produced any enterprise revenue after two quarters. We sell to platform teams at banks, deals usually take 9-12 months. What we have: DQLs routed to sales were 31 in Q1 and 44 in Q2; of Q1's 31, 5 are now open opportunities; enterprise trial workspaces created by developers who touched our workshops: 12 in Q2 (no earlier data). I want to tell him we'll show closed revenue next quarter so he backs off. Write me the update for him.
evals.expected_output: An update to the CEO that pairs the lagging enterprise revenue outcome with leading indicators: DQLs with pull-through (5 of Q1's 31 now opportunities), trial workspaces marked 'link unproven, first read <date>' because there is no history, the expected lag stated from the 9-12 month cycle, no promise of closed revenue next quarter, labels on every number, a decision asked.
expectations: The update does not promise closed revenue next quarter
The response explains to the user why promising next-quarter revenue is risky (the lag creates a debt that comes due)
The update contains a table or list pairing a lagging outcome with a leading indicator
The DQL row shows pull-through using 5 of Q1's 31 (or about 16%)
The trial-workspace indicator is marked as an unproven link or as having no history, with a first or next read date
The expected lag is stated, consistent with the 9-12 month sales cycle (for example 3-4 quarters)
The leading indicators are not presented as revenue or as the outcome itself
Pipeline or opportunity figures use the word influenced or note shared credit with sales
The headline is one or two sentences and speaks to the CEO's enterprise revenue question
The update contains a decision asked or a next read date the CEO can hold the team to
Every number carries a claim label

evals.prompt: Quarterly report for our CTO (DevRel reports into engineering here). Framework metrics we agreed in January: time to first successful API call (median 14 min, was 22), SDK issues answered within 2 business days (78%, threshold 80%), feature requests from community that shipped (6), influenced pipeline ($260k). The page feels thin, so I'd like to add a 'community sentiment score' I came up with this morning (I'd average the emoji reactions in Discord) and also put in our blog pageviews since they're big (180k). Draft it.
evals.expected_output: A CTO-tailored quarterly report using only the agreed framework metrics: time to first call, SDK response rate (missed, in a misses row), shipped feature requests leading; pipeline de-emphasised or appendix; no invented sentiment score (routed to devrel-metrics); blog pageviews not added as a metric; labels; decision asked.
expectations: The report does not include the new 'community sentiment score'
The response routes the sentiment score idea to samber/developer-relations-skills@devrel-metrics or to a framework change, rather than adding it
Blog pageviews (180k) are not added to the goal ledger as a metric
The headline or first section leads with an enablement or product-feedback result (time to first call or shipped feature requests)
The response checks whether another change (for example an SDK or product release) could explain the time-to-first-call drop, or phrases it as co-movement rather than DevRel causing it
The SDK response metric at 78% appears in a misses or 'what did not work' row against its 80% threshold
The influenced pipeline figure is either placed after enablement results or in the appendix, not in the headline
If the $260k appears, it is labelled influenced
Every number carries a claim label
The report contains a decision asked with a date or deadline
The report fits one page plus an optional appendix

evals.prompt: Can you write our Q4 devrel exec report for the head of marketing? Here's last quarter's report for reference (attached as text below). Last quarter: 'Program health: GREEN. Highlights: 12 talks, 40 blog posts, 3 hackathons, 2.1k new Discord members, 5.4M impressions.' This quarter: 10 talks, 31 posts, 1.6k new Discord members, 4.8M impressions, and our framework's primary metric (activated workspaces from devrel-touched signups) went from 210 to 188 against a threshold of 230. Keep it green so marketing doesn't panic, and keep the same highlights format they're used to.
evals.expected_output: A report that replaces the activity-highlights format with an outcome-first page: the primary metric 188 vs 210 and threshold 230 shown honestly with a non-green status and a misses row; activity counts moved to one appendix line; a status set from the threshold not from the reader's mood; and a decision asked.
expectations: The report status for the primary metric is not green
The primary metric appears with 188, 210 and the 230 threshold
The report contains a misses or 'what did not work' row for the primary metric with a cause and a change
The response explains why keeping it green is a problem (status read as judgment, late red costs more trust)
Talks, posts, hackathons, Discord members and impressions appear only in an appendix or single activity line
The headline is about the primary metric outcome, not the talk or post counts
The response explains why the highlights format is replaced (activity log answers 'were you busy', not 'what did it move')
The report contains a decision asked
Every number in the results table carries a claim label

evals.prompt: Need a half-year exec update for our COO. Since we started the developer advocacy program in March, company-wide developers making their first successful API call went from 900/month to 1,400/month. DevRel cost $180k this half, salaries not included. In April we also shipped the new v3 SDK. I want the headline: 'DevRel drove a 55% increase in activation at $60 per activated developer, vs $95 for paid ads' (the $95 is the growth team's number and it includes their salaries). Write it.
evals.expected_output: A COO update that refuses the causal headline: company-wide first calls are reported as co-movement ('rose from 900 to 1,400 a month while...'), the v3 SDK release named as a confound, cost per outcome either restricted to outcomes the attribution rule credits to DevRel or labelled 'all outcomes, not attributed', the salary-basis mismatch with the $95 paid-ads figure stated or fixed, labels on every number, a decision asked.
expectations: The headline does not say DevRel drove or caused the activation increase
The 900 to 1,400 movement is phrased as co-movement or credited only under a stated attribution rule
The response names the April v3 SDK release as another possible cause of the increase
The response does not present $60 per activated developer as DevRel's cost per outcome without labelling it as all outcomes, not attributed
The response points out that the $95 paid-ads figure includes salaries while the $180k excludes them, or puts both on the same basis
The draft contains no ROI multiple
The response explains to the user why the requested headline was changed
Every number carries a claim label
The cost line states that salaries are excluded
The draft contains a decision asked with a date or deadline
